description: Sanitize CLAUDECODE-family nesting env vars in the worker spawn command so interactive TUI workers boot when the tmux -L cam server was bootstrapped from inside a claude session.

userStories.title: Add WORKER_ENV_UNSET and env-prefix helper to implementer argv builder
userStories.description: As the supervisor spawning an implementer worker, I need the worker shell command to strip CLAUDECODE-family nesting env vars locally (via `env -u VAR ...` prefix) so an interactive claude TUI worker boots even when the tmux server inherited CLAUDECODE=1 from a parent claude session.
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts exports a canonical const WORKER_ENV_UNSET listing the nesting-detection env vars to strip: CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH, CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION, CLAUDECODE_ENTRYPOINT.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is NOT in WORKER_ENV_UNSET (worker must keep the same config dir); PATH is NOT in the list.
src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts exports a helper that renders the `env -u VAR1 -u VAR2 ... ` prefix string from WORKER_ENV_UNSET.

buildImplementerWorkerArgv prepends the env-prefix to the returned string so the result starts with `env -u CLAUDECODE` and contains `claude --permission-mode <mode> --session-id <uuid> --agent <name> '<prompt>'` after the prefix.

test/supervisor/worker-argv.test.ts is updated: any existing assertion that the result starts with `claude ` is replaced by an assertion that it starts with `env -u CLAUDECODE` and that `claude --permission-mode` appears after the env prefix.
test/supervisor/worker-argv.test.ts asserts CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is not present in the env-prefix.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts, test/supervisor/worker-argv.test.ts. The file is a pure string builder, no I/O. Keep the existing private shellEscape helper as-is; only prepend the env -u prefix to the returned argv string. The helper should be exported so review.ts can import it in US-002 without duplicating the list. Gotcha (lessons.md, 2026-06-12 CAM-42): respawn-pane inherits the tmux server's global env, so any nesting env left there poisons the worker pre-session; the fix is local to the worker shell string, not a mutation of the tmux server env. Repo invariant: NEVER add a --permission-mode flag on a cam subcommand (test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts); --permission-mode is only forwarded to the spawned claude inside the worker argv string.

userStories.title: Reuse env-prefix helper in reviewer argv builder
userStories.description: As the supervisor spawning a reviewer worker, I need buildReviewerWorkerArgv to apply the same `env -u ...` prefix as the implementer, importing the shared helper from worker-argv.ts so the list of stripped vars is defined once.
acceptanceCriteria: src/supervisor/review.ts imports WORKER_ENV_UNSET (and the env-prefix helper) from src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts and uses it inside buildReviewerWorkerArgv; no duplicated env-var list literal exists in review.ts.
buildReviewerWorkerArgv returns a string starting with `env -u CLAUDECODE` followed by `claude --permission-mode <mode> --session-id <uuid> --agent <name> '<prompt>'`.

test/supervisor/review.test.ts is updated: assertions that the interactive block starts with `claude --permission-mode` are replaced by assertions that it starts with `env -u CLAUDECODE` and that `claude --permission-mode` appears after the env prefix.
No regression in the existing review.test.ts coverage of session-id, agent flag, prompt escaping, and reviewer-specific behavior.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 having exported WORKER_ENV_UNSET and the env-prefix helper from src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts; do not start until US-001 passes:true. Files: src/supervisor/review.ts, test/supervisor/review.test.ts. review.ts currently has its own private shellEscape helper, keep that (the shared helper is the env-prefix one, not shellEscape). Confirm no other call sites build a claude worker argv string outside these two files; if a third one exists, flag it but do NOT fix in this story (out of scope). Gotcha: the reviewer is dispatched the same way as the implementer (interactive TUI via respawn-pane after CAM-42), so it has the same nesting-poison failure mode and needs the same fix.

userStories.title: Document trust-prompt block as a recovery scenario
userStories.description: As an operator running cam on a fresh project directory (CI, fresh clone, never-trusted folder), I need docs/recovery-runbook.md to document that the claude binary's `Quick safety check` / folder-trust prompt blocks the interactive TUI worker, the supervisor's sentinel poll cannot satisfy it, and how to recover.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/recovery-runbook.md gains a clearly-labeled scenario covering: symptom (worker pane stuck on `Quick safety check` / folder-trust prompt; sentinel poll eventually times out; transcript never starts growing), root cause (claude has never seen this project dir before), and mitigation (the normal `cam setup` flow has the human accept trust once; for a fresh dir accept via `tmux -L cam send-keys -t <worker-pane> Enter`, or pre-trust the folder).
No em-dash (—) anywhere in the edited markdown (project rule: use colon, comma, parens, period, or cut).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: docs/recovery-runbook.md. Pure docs story, no source change; typecheck/tests must still pass (sanity gate). Hard project rule (CLAUDE.md): no em-dash in persisted .md files. Place the new scenario alongside the existing scenarios; keep the existing structure (symptom / cause / fix) consistent with the rest of the runbook. Cross-link from the new scenario to the CAM-42 / CAM-43 context if the runbook already has a related section, but do not announce absence of unrelated content.

userStories.title: Operator validation: nested-tmux-server worker boot
userStories.description: As the operator validating CAM-43, I need to confirm that on a tmux `-L cam` server whose global env contains CLAUDECODE=1 (bootstrapped from inside a claude session) and WITHOUT running `tmux set-environment -g -u CLAUDECODE` by hand, a full `bun index.ts next` cycle on a throwaway story spawns a worker that boots into a live TUI / growing transcript instead of dying pre-session.
acceptanceCriteria: Operator captures evidence: `ps` output showing the worker process invoked as `env -u CLAUDECODE ... claude ...` (env-prefix observed in argv); transcript file mtime advancing for the worker session; pane reaches an interactive claude UI, NOT dead/empty.

Run is performed from a tmux server whose global env DOES contain CLAUDECODE=1 BEFORE the cycle starts (verify with `tmux -L cam show-environment -g | grep CLAUDECODE`), and WITHOUT manually unsetting it.
Evidence is documented in the journal or a CAM-43 follow-up note: the worker no longer dies pre-session in the nested scenario.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: none (validation only). Mirrors the CAM-42 US-006 ceremony. Requires real subscription claude + tmux + operator machine; cannot be automated. Pre-flight: ensure the cam binary is rebuilt (or `bun index.ts next` is used) so the new argv with env-prefix is actually exercised; lessons.md warns that a stale ~/.local/bin/cam can mask the fix. If the worker still dies pre-session, capture the pane history + the ps argv and reopen CAM-43 with the gap.
